description: Hot and Sour Soup is a quintessential Chinese comfort food, celebrated for its bold and complex flavor profile. This classic soup perfectly balances fiery chili heat with tangy vinegar, savory umami from mushrooms and pork, and a silky texture. It's a truly satisfying dish that warms the soul and awakens the palate with every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Mushrooms and Pork
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms according to package directions. Squeeze out excess water, remove stems from shiitake, and slice thinly. Slice pork tenderloin into thin strips.

instructions.title: Sauté Pork
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, add a splash of cooking oil over medium heat. Add the julienned pork and stir-fry until lightly browned. Remove the pork from the pot and set it aside.

instructions.title: Build the Soup Base
instructions.text: Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into the same pot. Add the rehydrated and sliced mushrooms, julienned bamboo shoots, and julienned firm tofu. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and let it cook for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Taste the soup and adjust the seasonings as needed, adding more vinegar for desired tartness or more white pepper for extra heat.

instructions.title: Thicken and Add Egg
instructions.text: Stir the cornstarch slurry (cornstarch mixed with cold water) well, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup while stirring constantly until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Next, slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while gently stirring the soup to create beautiful egg ribbons.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Return the cooked pork to the pot and stir to combine. Stir in the toasted sesame oil. Ladle the hot soup into individual bowls, garnish generously with chopped green onions, and a drizzle of chili oil if desired. Serve immediately and enjoy!

tips: For authentic flavor and texture, do not skip the dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms. Their earthy notes are crucial, and you can even add the strained mushroom soaking liquid to your broth for extra depth.

The balance of 'hot' (from white pepper and chili oil) and 'sour' (from rice vinegar) is the heart of this soup. Adjust these ingredients gradually to suit your personal preference, adding a little at a time until perfect.

To achieve delicate, silky egg ribbons, ensure your soup is at a gentle simmer, then pour the beaten eggs in a slow, thin stream while stirring the soup gently in a circular motion. Avoid vigorous stirring.
article:
Unleash a symphony of flavors in your kitchen with one of the most beloved and iconic dishes in Chinese cuisine: Hot and Sour Soup. This culinary masterpiece perfectly balances fiery spice with a tangy kick, all encapsulated in a rich, savory broth brimming with delightful textures. Far from being just a starter, Hot and Sour Soup is a complex, comforting, and deeply satisfying dish that has captivated palates worldwide. Whether you’re a seasoned chef or a curious home cook, mastering this classic will elevate your appreciation for authentic Chinese flavors.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

Hot and Sour Soup, known as "Suan La Tang" in Mandarin, is a staple in Chinese restaurants globally, particularly originating from the Sichuan and Hunan provinces, though variations exist throughout China. Its defining characteristics are, as the name suggests, its heat and its tang. The "hot" typically comes from white pepper and chili oil, while the "sour" is derived primarily from black vinegar. Beyond these foundational tastes, the soup boasts a complex umami depth from ingredients like dried shiitake mushrooms and often pork or chicken, all thickened to a luxurious consistency with cornstarch. It’s a hearty, warming bowl, often enjoyed as an appetizer but substantial enough to be a light meal, especially during colder months. Each spoonful offers a delightful interplay of savory broth, tender meat, crisp vegetables, and earthy mushrooms, making it an unforgettable experience.

## Ingredients for Hot and Sour Soup

Crafting the perfect Hot and Sour Soup begins with selecting the right ingredients. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need:

For the Broth:
*   6 cups chicken or vegetable broth (low sodium preferred)
*   2-3 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced (reserve mushroom liquid)

For the Soup Base & Protein:
*   4 oz lean pork loin or chicken breast, thinly sliced into matchsticks
*   1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cut into small matchsticks
*   1/2 cup bamboo shoots, thinly sliced
*   1/4 cup wood ear mushrooms (or more shiitake), rehydrated and thinly sliced
*   1 large egg, whisked

For Flavor & Seasoning:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce (light or regular)
*   2 tablespoons Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar is ideal)
*   1-2 tablespoons white pepper (adjust to desired heat)
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   Optional: 1-2 teaspoons chili oil or Sichuan peppercorns for extra heat

For Thickening:
*   3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons cold water (slurry)

For Garnish:
*   2 spring onions, green parts thinly sliced

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Hot and Sour Soup from scratch is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a delicious result:

1.  **Prepare Ingredients:** Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in warm water for at least 20 minutes. Squeeze out excess water, remove tough stems, and slice thinly. Slice pork/chicken, tofu, and bamboo shoots into matchsticks. Whisk the egg. Prepare the cornstarch slurry.
2.  **Cook Protein:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring the chicken or vegetable broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Add the sliced pork or chicken and cook for 2-3 minutes until just cooked through.
3.  **Add Vegetables & Mushrooms:** Stir in the rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and the reserved mushroom soaking liquid (strained, to avoid grit). Bring back to a simmer and cook for another 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
4.  **Season the Soup:** Add soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, and white pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings. This is where you can truly customize the "hot" and "sour" balance. If desired, add chili oil or Sichuan peppercorns for extra spice.
5.  **Thicken the Soup:** Slowly pour the cornstarch slurry into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Continue to stir until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. It should be viscous but still pourable.
6.  **Add Egg:** While stirring the soup in a circular motion, slowly drizzle in the whisked egg. The egg will cook into delicate ribbons.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the soup from heat. Stir in the sesame oil. Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into bowls and garnish generously with sliced spring onions. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup

Achieving restaurant-quality Hot and Sour Soup at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Balance is Key:** The beauty of this soup lies in the delicate balance of hot, sour, and savory. Don't be afraid to taste and adjust the white pepper and black vinegar throughout the cooking process. Add a little at a time until it's perfect for your palate.
*   **Quality Black Vinegar:** Invest in good quality Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar). Its complex, malty, and slightly sweet flavor is crucial for the authentic sourness. Regular white vinegar won't provide the same depth.
*   **White Pepper Power:** White pepper is the traditional "heat" source for this soup, offering a different kind of warmth than chili. Don't skimp on it, but also be mindful of its pungency.
*   **Velvety Texture:** When adding the cornstarch slurry, ensure the soup is at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. Pour slowly and stir continuously to prevent lumps and achieve a smooth, silky texture. For the egg ribbons, pour slowly into a swirling soup; avoid stirring vigorously immediately after adding the egg, which can break up the ribbons.
*   **Freshness Matters:** While dried mushrooms are essential for depth, fresh ingredients for the vegetables and protein will make a noticeable difference in flavor and texture.
*   **Customizing Heat:** For more heat, add dried chili flakes, a dash of chili oil, or a pinch of ground Sichuan peppercorns along with the white pepper.

## Serving Suggestions

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **As an Appetizer:** This is its most common role, served before a larger Chinese meal. Its bold flavors awaken the palate.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with some plain white rice or a simple side of steamed vegetables, a hearty bowl of Hot and Sour Soup can be a satisfying and flavorful light lunch or dinner.
*   **Alongside Dim Sum:** It makes a fantastic accompaniment to an array of dim sum dishes, cutting through richer flavors with its tang and spice.
*   **With Noodles:** For a more substantial meal, add some thin egg noodles or rice vermicelli directly to the soup bowl.
*   **Winter Warmer:** There's nothing quite like a steaming bowl of Hot and Sour Soup to chase away the chill on a cold day, providing warmth from the inside out.

## Variations & Substitutions

The beauty of Chinese cuisine often lies in its adaptability. Hot and Sour Soup is no exception:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Easily make this soup vegetarian by using vegetable broth and omitting the pork/chicken. For a vegan version, also omit the egg. You can add extra tofu, more varieties of mushrooms (enoki, oyster), or even rehydrated textured vegetable protein (TVP) for added substance.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Ensure your soy sauce is gluten-free (tamari) and check that your broth and other seasonings do not contain hidden gluten.
*   **Protein Swaps:** Instead of pork or chicken, you can use shrimp, thinly sliced beef, or even rehydrated dried scallops for a different flavor profile.
*   **Mushroom Variety:** Experiment with different types of mushrooms. Fresh shiitake, enoki, or oyster mushrooms can be added for varied textures and earthy notes.
*   **Extra Vegetables:** Feel free to add other quick-cooking vegetables like shredded carrots, snow peas, or spinach for added nutrients and color.
*   **Regional Differences:** Some regional versions might include ingredients like preserved mustard greens, blood curd, or even more fermented elements, offering distinct flavor nuances.

Embrace the vibrant world of Chinese soups and stews by trying your hand at this iconic Hot and Sour Soup. Its dynamic flavors, comforting warmth, and customizable nature make it a truly rewarding dish to prepare and savor. Get ready to impress your taste buds and your guests with this authentic culinary delight!
